Guidance & outlook: 4.5 crores in quarter 4, but slight positive in quarter 1 FY26.
2,000 SPSF in the festive quarter, and that is the internal target.
So overall, I would say for Spencer's, the outlook for FY '27 is to continue and sustain this growth momentum.
Growth & demand: 416 crores in quarter 1 last year, which is a 13% year -on-year growth.
This overall performance of 13% sales growth was powered by strong 8% growth, which w as on the Spencer's format.
On Nature Basket, we had a slightly muted performance, 8% quarter -on-quarter growth versus Q4 and a 13% degrowth.
Margins & costs: And there was a 2x improvement as far as our EBITDA was concerned.
If I look for like -for-like, margins are steady at 19%.
Our store EBITDA, which is the true barometer of efficiency has actually reached, we don't disclose that, but it's actually 2x of what it was in quarter 1 of last year.
Capex & expansion: I think from here on, we will see continuous growth and growth with continued control on our operating costs will be the expansion lever as far as EBITDA is concerned.
We are being very calibrated in our customer acquisition.
Most of our customer acquisition is Spencer's Retail Limited August 13, 2026 coming from our existing offline customers who choose this platform and, therefore, tend to have higher stickiness.
Balance sheet & cash: We are looking at continued discipline when it comes to our working capital allocation and inventory optimization, focusing on availability of the right SKUs, continuing to build on our membership pro gram and drive the online in a calibrated, but in a, I would say, aggressive manner in terms of growth.
So, at a consol level, we have a total debt of Rs.
And I just wanted to check this -- a large part of the debt was supposed to get refinanced in this current year.
Risks & challenges: But I mean, given all the other challenges which we had around availability, range optimization, we were not able to dial up the consumer acquisition piece of it.

Q1 EBITDA at Rs18 crs (4.4% of Sales) vs Rs14.6 crs (4.2% of sales) in Q1 LY.
